correctness.rationale: The six-bit truth table has exactly 15 possible four-output words, excluding `1100`. The five-bit truth table for Rule 184 after reflected Rule 226 has precisely four mismatch windows 01100, 11000, 11001, 11100, each and collectively equivalent to occurrence of `1100` on a ring. Thus necessity and sufficiency hold at every size, including short rings. Unborderedness makes length-four occurrences nonoverlapping; cyclic-block spacing yields the exact inclusion–exclusion with fixed weight. A four-state prefix-suffix automaton gives trace(A(u)^n), determinant 1-(1+u)z+u^2z^4, and resulting generating function, recurrence and asymptotics. Replayed standalone standard-library verifier returns VERIFY_OK; finite checks cover all length-1..13 rings and matrix inclusion-exclusion agreement through length 18. The proof supplies all-length quantifiers independent of finite experiments.

Neither examined primary text gives the exact cyclic one-step image language, the equivalence F∘G=identity on that image, or the fixed-weight reachable-state enumeration. The generalized fact that CA images are sofic or finite-type in special cases is insufficient by itself to give this four-letter obstruction and explicit section. value.rationale: The classical traffic-automaton inverse problem for a prescribed complete circular post-update state at fixed particle density is natural in finite dynamical systems and traffic modeling. A four-bit local obstruction provides a sharp existence criterion, reflected Rule 226 constructs a predecessor locally in one step, and density-refined exact state counts quantify the accessible phase space at each ring size. These structural all-length results are substantively stronger than routine enumeration and do not rely on a chosen artificial finite slice.
